_doc: Bolivia, the zones of the cross-border recommended trips (Peru & Bolivia, Atacama & Uyuni), written by hand from the sources of each area. Same format as pe.json.

areas.season: At 3,640 m: dry and sunny May to October with nights near freezing in June and July; rain most afternoons December to March.
areas.sleep: In the centre around Calle Sagárnaga and the San Francisco church, or quieter Sopocachi. The airport is up in El Alto at 4,060 m.

items.name: The city from the cable cars
items.best: Late afternoon, for the light on Illimani
items.why: The world's biggest urban cable-car network: ride the red and yellow lines up to El Alto and the whole bowl of La Paz opens under the snow of Illimani.

items.name: Witches' Market, San Francisco and Plaza Murillo
items.why: Dried llama foetuses and herbs for offerings to Pachamama, a baroque church carved with Andean motifs, and the square of the presidential palace.

items.name: Tiwanaku ruins
items.book: A day ahead with a La Paz agency, with a guide
items.why: The capital of a civilisation older than the Incas, 70 km from La Paz: the Gate of the Sun and the stone heads of the semi-underground temple. On UNESCO's list.

items.name: Valle de la Luna
items.why: A maze of clay spires eroded by the rain, twenty minutes below the city, on a short marked loop.

items.name: Mountain bike down the Death Road
items.book: Only with an operator with good bikes and guides, a few days ahead
items.why: From the snow of La Cumbre at 4,650 m down 3,500 m of gravel road cut into the cliff to the jungle of the Yungas. Downhill all day, from a puffer to a T-shirt.
extras: It starts near freezing and ends at 25 °C: layers you can stuff in the support van.
Stay on the inside of the road and slow on the corners: the drop is real.
La Paz is high: the first day, walk slowly, drink a lot of water and coca tea, eat light.
Saturday and Sunday the El Alto market at 16 de Julio is one of the biggest in South America.
On Sunday evenings the cholitas wrestle in El Alto: touristy, and fun.

areas.season: On Lake Titicaca at 3,840 m: strong sun, cold nights all year, rain in the afternoon December to March.
areas.sleep: In Copacabana near the lake, or one night in a lodge on Isla del Sol for the sunset and the stars.

items.name: Isla del Sol by boat
items.book: Boat tickets at the Copacabana pier the day before
items.why: The island where the Incas placed the birth of the Sun: terraces, eucalyptus, the Inca stairway at Yumani and the ruins of Pilko Kaina above a deep blue lake.

steps.what: Up the Inca stairway to Yumani
Pilko Kaina ruins and the views over the lake
Lunch with lake trout in Yumani

extras: Which parts of the island are open changes with local disputes: ask at the pier before you buy.
Each community on the island charges a small entrance fee: carry cash in bolivianos.

items.name: Sunset from Cerro Calvario
items.why: A steep path of stations of the cross above the town; at the top the whole lake turns gold.

items.name: The basilica and the blessing of the cars
items.why: Bolivia's most loved shrine, white and Moorish; outside, priests bless decorated cars with flowers and beer.

extras: From Puno the bus crosses the border at Kasani in about 3 hours; from La Paz it crosses the Strait of Tiquina on a small ferry.
Copacabana's lake trout (trucha) is the dish: grilled, on the waterfront stalls.

areas.season: At 3,660 m: sunny and dry from April to November, with nights down to −15 °C in June to August. From January to March rain floods the salt flat into a mirror, and some tracks close.
areas.sleep: In Uyuni town, or in a hotel built of salt at the edge of the flat near Colchani.

items.name: The salt flat by 4x4, to Incahuasi and the sunset
items.book: A day ahead with an Uyuni agency; check the jeep and the driver's reviews
items.why: The biggest salt flat on Earth, white to the horizon: the train cemetery, the salt workers of Colchani, cactus island Incahuasi in the middle, and the sun going down on the salt.

steps.what: Onto the salt: the old salt hotel and the flags

extras: The salt reflects the sun: dark glasses and sun cream even on the chin and under the nose.
Funny perspective photos: bring a small toy or a bottle as a prop.

items.name: The salt flat as a mirror
items.book: With an Uyuni agency, the day before
items.why: After the rains a few centimetres of water turn the flat into a mirror of the sky, with no line between them.

items.name: Stars and sunrise on the salt
items.book: With an Uyuni agency, the day before
items.why: No light for a hundred kilometres: the Milky Way over the white, then the sun coming up.
extras: Before dawn it can be −15 °C: the warmest you have, gloves and a hat.
Flights to La Paz leave from Uyuni's small airport; the night bus takes about 9 hours.
Cash in bolivianos: cards work in few places in Uyuni.

names: Eduardo Avaroa Andean Fauna National Reserve
areas.season: Between 4,200 and 4,900 m: sunny days, strong wind in the afternoon, frost every night; down to −20 °C in the shelters in June to August. Snow or storms can close the tracks from January to March.
areas.sleep: Basic shared shelters: near Laguna Colorada at about 4,300 m, no heating; the second night in a village or a salt hotel near the salt flat. A sleeping bag rated −10 °C, or rent one in San Pedro or Uyuni.

items.name: Laguna Verde, the Dalí desert, Polques and Laguna Colorada
items.hours: The first day of the jeep tour
items.best: Leave San Pedro around 07:00 for the border
items.book: A 3-day jeep tour San Pedro to Uyuni, a few days ahead, driver and cook included
items.why: Into Bolivia at the Hito Cajón border: a green lake under the cone of Licancabur, rocks that look painted by Dalí, a hot pool at 4,400 m, then a red lake full of flamingos.

steps.what: Pick-up in San Pedro, up to the Bolivian border

steps.note: breakfast while the papers are done

steps.what: Laguna Blanca and Laguna Verde under Licancabur

steps.note: bring a swimsuit and a towel

steps.what: Shelter near the lake, dinner by the cook

sights: Eduardo Avaroa Andean Fauna National Reserve

items.name: Sol de Mañana at dawn, Árbol de Piedra and the high lagoons
items.hours: The second day of the jeep tour
items.why: Boiling mud and steam vents at 4,900 m in the first light, the rock tree of the Siloli desert, then a chain of lagoons with flamingos below volcanoes, to a night at the edge of the salt.
extras: Keep to the hard ground: the crust around the pools is thin.
Do this after a few days at San Pedro's 2,400 m or in La Paz: the night at 4,300 m is the hardest part of the trip.
Bring water, snacks, cash for the park entrance and the hot springs, and a power bank: the shelters have little electricity.
